text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated egress packet loss detected from edge-pop us-east1 -> carrier-AS4321. Metric alert: pop.egress.pkt_loss_us-east1 > 10% for 3m. Auto-page: #incidents net-oncall.

net-oncall: I'm on it. Observed 10-18% loss to a handful of prefixes via transit peer AS4321, started ~09:03 UTC. CDN egress LB shows increased RTOs.

sre_alex: Confirming customer-facing error rate? Any 5xx spikes or timeouts in the API gateway? @support_emma please chime in.

support_emma: Seeing a cluster of tickets from two customers in us-east region complaining about slow responses and occasional 504s since ~09:05. Correlates with synthetic pings showing high retransmits.

infra_june: Routing table shows repeated BGP updates from peer AS4321 for our ecmp-set-12. Possible misannounce or partial packet-drop inside carrier path. Traceroute from pop->carrier shows hops timing out consistently at carrier edge:

```
traceroute to 198.51.100.45 (198.51.100.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.4.0.1  0.8 ms  0.7 ms  0.6 ms
 2  192.0.2.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.1  65 ms  64 ms  66 ms
```

infra_june: Looks like packet loss starts at hop 3 which maps to carrier PE.

eng_runtime: Any automatic fallback active? Are we failingover to other POPs per routing policy? @net-oncall what's the health of us-east2 and us-west1 for this traffic class?

net-oncall: We currently have active steering but traffic share to backups is low because ECMP still prefers the AS4321 path for majority of prefixes. us-east2 is healthy; we can accelerate steering by withdrawing specific prefixes from us-east1 and re-advertising via us-east2.

sre_alex: Plan: 1) Deprecate problematic routes from us-east1 for affected prefix set (small prefix list) 2) Trigger traffic steer to us-east2 via lower MED/AS-path prepends 3) Notify customers and update support tickets 4) Continue monitoring and coordinate with carrier rep. Any objections?

support_emma: +1. I'll update affected customer tickets with a short note and ETA after the steer.

infra_june: Ready to run withdraw and prepends. Proposed command sequence (on edge-router us-east1):
```
# withdraw prefixes in reflect-map "AS4321-problematic-list"
configure terminal
router bgp 65012
no network 203.0.113.0/24 route-map AS4321-block
neighbor 198.51.100.2 shutdown (if soft withdraw needed)
exit
```

infra_june: Or we can apply local-prepend toward transit TLs to reduce preference without full withdraw. Soft approach first.

net-oncall: Will apply 2x prepend to AS-path on transit egress for the affected prefixes, monitor for 5 minutes, then withdraw if no improvement. Executing now.

incident-bot: Action logged: net-oncall executed bgp as-path prepend for prefix list AS4321-problematic-list at 09:18 UTC.

infra_june: After prepend, observed drop in loss to 3-5% within 60s for test flows — traffic shifted to us-east2 path. Latency to test IP improved ~45ms -> ~28ms.

support_emma: Updated support: "We're seeing packet loss on a carrier path and have steered traffic to alternate POPs. Some customers may see transient errors for the next 30-60 minutes. We will follow up once stable."

eng_runtime: Any downstream cache invalidation or session-affecting changes? We might see session affinity issues for websocket sessions. Recommend flagging long-lived sessions and offering reconnect guidance in customers notifications.

sre_alex: Good call — add note to customer message. Also enable increased retries on edge LB (2->4) temporarily for health tests and downstream callers.

net-oncall: LB retry bumped for us-east1 -> now 4, applied at 09:22 UTC.

incident-bot: Pager cleared for net-oncall at 09:40 UTC. Incident status: mitigated (traffic steered). Monitoring for regression for next 2h.

sre_lee: Taking over monitoring & follow-ups for next shift. Handoff: I have context and the commands used. Will maintain comms with carrier and customer_ops. @customer_ops please coordinate any customer escalations overnight.

customer_ops: Acknowledged. We'll prepare a short post-incident note for customers in the morning and collect a list of impacted prefixes + time windows.

sre_alex: Postmortem items: - Confirm root cause with carrier (misroute vs link hardware) - Improve automation for quick prefix withdraws for partial failures - Add synthetic checks from edge egress to transits and set lower thresholds for packetloss alerting - Document websocket reconnect guidance.

net-oncall: Logging commands and outputs to the incident ticket. Will attach bgp update stream and traceroutes.

support_emma: Customers kept in the loop. No escalations to SEs needed as of now.

sre_lee: Closing active mitigation. Keeping this thread open for notes. If any regression, ping me @sre_lee. :thumbsup:
